_about: Base-case forecast assumptions, FY2025-FY2029. Every value has a rationale and the evidence behind it. Only information public by the 31 Jan 2025 valuation date is used. Edit a value here and re-run `python -m src.forecast`.

warehouses.rationale: FY2025: management plans 29 openings including 3 relocations, so 26 net (Q1 FY2025 10-Q). FY2026-29: 27 a year, the average of FY2024 actual (29) and FY2025 plan (26). This is above the FY2021-23 pace of 20-23 because the opening pipeline has accelerated.
evidence: Q1 FY2025 10-Q: 7 opened in Q1, 22 more planned

comparable_sales_growth.rationale: Reported comps, including gasoline and FX. Q1 FY2025 total comps were 5% (7% excl. gas & FX; lower gas prices and a stronger dollar held the reported number back). FY2025 is set at 5.5%, assuming these headwinds ease a little. The rate then fades to 4.0% by FY2028: roughly 2-2.5% inflation plus 1.5-2% traffic and market-share gains. That is below the FY2023-24 ex-gas/FX run-rate of 5-6% and the FY2016-19 pre-pandemic average of about 5%, because a larger base makes high comps harder to sustain.
evidence: Q1 FY2025 comps 5% / 7% ex gas & FX

new_warehouse_productivity.rationale: New warehouses open below the fleet average and ramp up over several years. Historically, net sales growth not explained by comps was about 0.6-0.7x net unit growth (FY2021 0.66, FY2022 0.70, FY2023 0.63, FY2024 0.60). Growth from new warehouses = 0.65 x net unit growth.

paid_member_growth.rationale: Year-end paid members grew 6-8% a year in FY2021-24, averaging 7.0%, and were up 7.5% year on year at Q1 FY2025 (77.4m vs 72.0m). Growth fades toward 5% as more new warehouses open in existing markets, which lowers the member uplift per opening (a point the 10-Q itself makes).

membership_fee_increase.rationale: Effective 1 Sep 2024, the U.S./Canada Gold Star and Business fee rose from $60 to $65 (+8.3%) and the Executive fee from $120 to $130 (+8.3%), as disclosed in the FY2024 10-K. Affected share = 85%, a proxy based on U.S. and Canada being 86% of revenue (Costco does not split fee income by segment). Fees are recognized over the 12-month membership term and renewals are spread across the year, so about half the uplift lands in FY2025 and the rest in FY2026. Net effect: fee per member +3.5% in FY2025 and +3.5% in FY2026.

fee_per_member_other_growth.rationale: Apart from fee increases, fee income per average paid member was flat at about $65-66 in FY2021-24: more Executive upgrades were offset by growth in lower-fee international members. The next fee increase (historically every 5.5-7 years: 2011, 2017, 2024) would fall around FY2030-31, after the explicit forecast, so it is not included. It is an upside to the terminal value.

gross_margin_on_net_sales.rationale: FY2024 was 10.92%. Q1 FY2025 rose 24bp year on year (7bp excluding gasoline deflation), helped by core merchandise mix and the co-branded credit card. The model holds 11.0%, at the upper end of the FY2020-24 range (10.5-11.2%). The model assumes no further expansion because Costco reinvests margin in price, and the higher Executive reward cap ($1,250 from $1,000) is a small cost.
evidence: Q1 FY2025 10-Q gross margin ex gas 11.11%

sga_pct_net_sales.rationale: FY2024 was 9.14%. Q1 FY2025 was 14bp higher year on year, flat excluding gasoline deflation. The model holds 9.20%: wage investment and technology spend offset further operating leverage. This deliberately assumes no additional SG&A leverage, even though SG&A fell from 10.0% to 9.1% of net sales over FY2020-24.

tax_rate.rationale: Effective rate excluding discrete items was 25.9-26.6% in FY2020-24 (26.4% in FY2024). Recurring stock-compensation deductions trim a few tenths off in most years, so the model uses 26.0% on both NOPAT and net income.

d_and_a_pct_beginning_ppe.rationale: D&A as a share of beginning net PP&E was 8.2%, 8.1%, 8.4% and 8.4% in FY2021-24. Linking D&A to the asset base keeps capex and depreciation consistent.

capex.rationale: FY2025: management's stated plan of about $5.0bn (Q1 FY2025 10-Q). FY2026-29: 1.85% of revenue, in line with FY2021-24 (1.71-1.85%) and consistent with about 27 openings a year plus remodels, depots and technology.

working_capital_pct_revenue.rationale: Each operating working-capital line is held at its FY2024 ratio to revenue. Deferred membership fees are held at their ratio to fee income. Together this gives operating working capital of about -4.8% of revenue, so growth releases cash. FY2024 levels are used rather than the FY2020-21 pandemic years (about -6%).

interest.rationale: Interest expense stays at the FY2024 level ($169m) because debt is held flat and the senior notes are fixed-rate. Interest income is a yield on beginning-of-year cash and short-term investments, with no circular reference. FY2024 earned 4.1% on beginning balances. Yields step down from 3.5% to 3.0% after the Fed's Sep-Dec 2024 rate cuts.
evidence: FY2024 interest income and other $624m on $15.2bn beginning cash & investments

capital_structure.debt: held flat at the FY2024 level (maturities refinanced)
capital_structure.leases_and_other_long_term_items: held flat at the FY2024 level
capital_structure.rationale: Regular payout was 26-30% of EPS in FY2020-24. No special dividends are assumed, so excess cash builds on the balance sheet. That does not change enterprise value in the DCF. Buybacks of $700m a year match FY2024 and roughly offset stock-compensation dilution, so diluted shares stay flat at the Q1 FY2025 count. None of these financing assumptions affect the unlevered DCF. They are used to balance the three statements.

known_simplifications: Forecast is on a 52-week basis. FY2028 will be a 53-week year (ending 3 Sep 2028), which adds about 2% to that year's sales. It is excluded so year-over-year growth rates stay comparable.
PP&E rolls forward as beginning + capex - D&A. Historically, disposals and FX left actual PP&E about $0.1-0.8bn below this roll-forward.
Other comprehensive income (FX translation) is not forecast.
